page: Microsoft Azure L24aos_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Laosv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD processor, paired with 192.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

A primary characteristic of this server is its substantial local storage capacity of 17,281 GB, which is Premium Storage capable. This large local storage footprint is bundled directly with the instance, supporting high-capacity local data requirements. The instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or onboard GPU hardware.

From a resource density perspective, the L24aos_v5 offers a high ratio of local storage and memory relative to its 24 dedicated compute cores. The lack of integrated GPU accelerators and advanced CPU instruction sets represents a tradeoff, limiting its utility for hardware-accelerated machine learning or specialized vector math workloads. However, the high density of local storage and memory provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require large data footprints close to the processor without relying on external network-attached storage.

The hardware profile of the L24aos_v5 makes it suitable for large-scale database deployments, memory-intensive data processing, local storage caching, and enterprise applications requiring substantial local disk space and a 1:8 memory-to-vCPU ratio.
